concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
question: In which order did Mendeleev arrange the elements in his periodic table?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Increasing atomic mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the elements in his periodic table based on their **increasing atomic mass**.
 
• He grouped elements with similar chemical properties into vertical columns called **groups**.
 
• Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table to **predict the existence of undiscovered elements** and their properties.
 
• The periodic table was published in **1869**, marking a significant advancement in the study of chemistry.
 
• Although atomic mass was the primary criterion, Mendeleev occasionally altered the arrangement to ensure elements with similar properties were aligned correctly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table:**

 
 
• A tabular arrangement of chemical elements organized by their **atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties**.
 
• The modern periodic table is based on the **Moseley’s concept of increasing atomic number**, rather than atomic mass.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• The total mass of protons and neutrons in an atom's nucleus.
 
• Mendeleev used atomic mass as a criterion because atomic numbers were unknown at the time.
 
 
 
• **Predictions Made by Mendeleev:**
 
 
• Mendeleev successfully predicted the properties of elements like **gallium (eka-aluminum)** and **germanium (eka-silicon)**.
 
• These predictions were later confirmed with the discovery of these elements.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Mendeleev’s Table:**
 
 
• Some elements were placed out of order based on atomic mass to align with chemical properties.
 
• The periodic table did not account for the existence of **isotopes**, which have the same atomic number but different atomic masses.
